title: Why does a game become famous?
text: Every year thousands of video games are published, but only a few become really famous. What is the difference? Experts who study games have found some common ingredients.

The first ingredient is a simple idea that anyone can understand in a few seconds. Tetris, which was made in 1984, only has falling pieces. Among Us, where players look for a traitor, can be explained in one sentence.

The second ingredient is friends. A game that you can play with other people spreads much faster. When a player who loves a game invites a friend, the friend often invites more friends. This is called the network effect.

The third ingredient is the internet. Streamers and YouTubers, who have millions of followers, can make a game famous overnight. Among Us came out in 2018, but it only became a hit in 2020, when famous streamers started to play it.

Finally, luck plays a part. Many excellent games never find their audience, while some strange ones go viral. That is why game studios often say that a hit is a mix of a good idea, good timing and a little magic.

grammar.title: Grammar: relative clauses
grammar.rule: Use who for people, which for things and where for places. That can be used for people and things.
rows: a game where you look for a traitor
items: Streamers ___ have millions of followers are powerful.
Tetris is a game ___ was made in 1984.
Among Us is a game ___ players look for a traitor.
A player ___ loves a game invites friends.
This is the studio ___ made the game.
